title: 'Opening Match Blowout': Silva's 52% Attack Efficiency More Welcomed Than Her 27 Points; GS Caltex's Coach Lee Young-tak Highlights "Mutual Growth" [Jangchung On-Site] - 스타뉴스
content:
As expected, they delivered. Seoul GS Caltex smiled from the opening match with a more solidified roster. GS Caltex, led by Coach Lee Young-tak, secured a decisive 3-0 (25-18, 25-21, 25-22) victory in the set score against Gimcheon Korea Expressway Corporation in the opening match of the 2026-2027 HK Hwaseung Life V-League Women's Division, held at Jangchung Gymnasium in Jung-gu, Seoul, on the 31st. Although they were rated as the top championship contender after winning both the title as defending champions and the Cup tournament, the result exceeded expectations. Opposite spiker Gizel Silva (registered name: Silva) exploded for a team-high 27 points, achieving an attack success rate of up to 60%. She accounted for 40% of the team's attacks. Newly joined Asian quota player Tanacha Sooksot (registered name: Tanacha) scored 13 points, while rapidly growing Kwon Min-ji poured in 11 points. The team secured a blowout victory by effectively utilizing Choi Ga-eun (7 points) and Oh Se-yeon (5 points) from the middle. Before the game, Coach Lee cited the opponent's defense as a strength and stated, "Rather than hitting hard while accepting unforced errors, we will find a solution by attacking with both long and short balls," and this strategy worked perfectly. There were four service aces, but most importantly, it was effective in properly shaking up the opponent's powerful weapon, the receiving line. Korea Expressway Corporation's receiving efficiency was limited to 30.88%, resulting in a failure to establish proper attack connections. Conversely, GS Caltex, based on stable receiving (efficiency of 44.64%), deployed various attacks and secured an easy victory. Coach Lee Young-tak, met after the game, praised the team, saying, "It was a very well-played game. I did not expect to win so one-sidedly," adding, "The players seem to have managed their bodies and adjusted their condition well during the two weeks following the KOVO Cup." Korea Expressway Corporation took the lead by changing the outside hitter position with Park Jeong-a in the second set and Kang So-hwi in the third set, but ultimately could not stop GS Caltex's momentum. Coach Lee expressed satisfaction, stating, "During the two games in the KOVO Cup, we experienced all of Korea Expressway Corporation's outside hitter combinations," and continued, "We analyzed that and prepared accordingly. I thought that if anyone came in, as long as we did our part, we would have a good game. The analysis and preparation matched well, and the players quickly adapted to the opponent's substitutions, leading to a good performance." Kwon Min-ji's growth is astonishing. Following her performances in last season's championship finals and the Cup tournament, she delivered a surprising display from the new season's opening match. Coach Lee gave a thumbs up, saying, "She has many assets, but there have been ups and downs. She gained a lot of confidence during the championship finals, and although she wavered early in the KOVO Cup, she performed incredibly in the final. Her own rhythm was good. That momentum carried over well into the opening match." Not only Kwon Min-ji, but also Tanacha's joining and the growth of middle blockers reduced the offensive burden on Silva. Coach Lee smiled and said, "Just looking at today's game, Kim Ji-won did a great job with distribution and management. As a result, Silva could receive focused marking from the opponent more comfortably; there were several instances of one-blocker coverage and even 1.5-blocker coverage today," adding, "It will become easier for Silva to play. There is good penetration from the outside, but as receiving stabilizes and middle attacks are mixed in, it seems they can execute diverse plays." Stable receiving, relaxed game management, and teammates who effectively finish scoring on the opposite side. Silva, whose career attack efficiency is 29.75%, achieved an attack efficiency of a whopping 52.5% today. With her teammates contributing strength, Silva was able to attack in a much more comfortable situation, inevitably leading to higher efficiency. Of course, GS Caltex is ultimately a team that cannot be explained without Silva. Only by sharing the burden with other players on days like this can Silva conserve stamina and use her power effectively during games and throughout the season. Coach Lee expressed confidence, stating, "When it's time to use her, she must be used. Although she has aged another year, she manages herself very well, and since the training department has been working with us for four years, I believe they have sufficient manuals for management. If managed according to those manuals, she will be able to perform well until the end." <© STARNEWS. All rights reserved. Korea Expressway Corporation Hi-Pass will play its opening match against HK Heungkuk Financial 2026–2027 V-League Women's Division GS Caltex at Jangchung Gymnasium on the 31st. Two days before the opening. The Expressway Corporation appointed acting coach Kim Young-rae as the official head coach. Before last year's championship finals, the Expressway Corporation announced a split with head coach Kim Jong-min and handed the reins to then-chief coach Kim Young-rae. After losing to GS Caltex in the championship finals, the team successfully advanced to the finals of the cup tournament. However, they were once again defeated by GS Caltex, leaving them with regret. Nevertheless, Kim, who was highly praised for stabilizing and leading the team, was officially appointed as head coach. Coach Kim, who will make his debut as official head coach on the 31st, said, "I'm very nervous. I'm also excited. I've prepared well, so I want to help the players do their best." Comparing his previous role as acting coach to his current position, Kim stated, "Being the official head coach is much more nerve-wracking. The first button is the most important. It's the start of the season and my first time as a head coach. I'm very nervous, but I trust the players." Regarding his volleyball philosophy, he emphasized, "We must avoid unforced errors. If players are not in position and fail to set the ball, it dampens the team's morale. I've talked a lot about this. I hope the team never gives up. My biggest challenge is to build a team that fans see as passionate and tenacious on the court." To win the debut match, they must overcome the 'defending champions' GS Caltex. GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek said, "Kim Young-rae is a close junior I played with during my career. His first match as acting coach was also against us. title: 2024 BMW F 900 GS Buyer’s Guide [Specs, Price] - Ultimate Motorcycling
content: The 2024 BMW F 900 GS replaces the F 850 GS and turns the middleweight GS into a more off-road-capable adventure bike, while the new F 800 GS takes over the street-focused role. The F 900 GS weighs 31 pounds less than the 850, much of it trimmed high or far from the center of gravity. The 3.8-gallon plastic fuel tank alone is 10 pounds lighter than the old steel tank, and the rear subframe, Akrapovič muffler, and LED headlight are lighter, too. Curb weight is 483 pounds. A handlebar raised 0.6 inches, footpegs lowered 0.8 inches, and a slimmer tank and tail make the GS feel like a big dirt bike when standing. The 34.3-inch seat height is tall; optional Rallye seats lower it 1.4 inches or raise it 0.8 inches. The 895cc parallel twin from the F 900 R and F 900 XR makes 105 horsepower and 69 ft-lbs of torque, 10 horsepower more than the 850. A 270/450-degree firing order gives it a pleasant throb instead of a buzz, and the GS is stable and comfortable on long freeway stints. A fully adjustable 43mm Showa inverted fork and a ZF shock with rebound damping and hydraulic spring-preload adjustment provide about nine inches of travel at each end. The suspension is compliant without being soft and stays balanced off-road. The $1495 Enduro Package Pro adds a fully adjustable 45mm Showa fork, a fully adjustable Sachs ZF shock, and a taller handlebar. Twin 305mm front discs with two-piston Brembo calipers have a soft initial bite that suits the dirt. Road and Rain ride modes are standard. The $1750 Premium Package adds Dynamic, Enduro, and Enduro Pro modes, a quickshifter, cruise control, keyless ride, GPS prep, and tire-pressure monitoring. Enduro Pro is the dirt mode, with strong, linear throttle response, minimal traction control, and front-only ABS. title: Bullish Options Trades Slow amid AI Uncertainty - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Options markets are showing signs of increased nervousness about artificial intelligence (AI) as investors focus closely on earnings from large tech companies and try to separate likely winners from losers, says Lee Coppersmith from the Equity Derivative Sales team in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. Overall demand for AI stocks remains strong and the S&P has remained resilient, but put option buying has picked up in recent weeks while activity has waned in call options that would reward a jump in equities, he explains on The Markets podcast. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Thursday, October 29th, and I'm here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Lee Coppersmith, who is on our hedge fund derivative sales desk within FICC and Equities. And we're going to be talking about everything that's current right now, the Fed, earnings, AI, the retail investors, vol, the whole shebang. Lee, thanks so much for joining us. Chris Hussey: Okay, Lee, let's start with the Fed, one of the big pieces of news that came out this week. What did we learn? What was the market's reaction? Lee Coppersmith: So stepping back, I think when you look at the setup heading into the Fed, the S&P options market was implying somewhere between a 60 and 65 basis point move. That's a bit lower than we've seen going into the previous FOMC meetings, somewhere around, call it 75 basis points. So I think the focus on the Fed was actually kind of like secondhand relative to the earnings that we're kind of digesting around it. Mainly, I think this is because you weren't really expecting a decision from them yesterday. So overall, I think Warsh and the committee struck this balanced tone, but there was a little bit of apprehension, I think, in the way they conveyed their message, particularly around the correlation between interest rates and the AI story, which I think kind of suggested they are happy to go at a slower pace. The equity markets actually digested this all very well. This was the first time in seven meetings that the S&P actually finished up on the day after an FOMC press conference. So I think all things considered, it was a sigh of relief after we've seen multiple press conferences in a row inject some kind of volatility into the equity space. Chris Hussey: Well, it's always great to get a little bit of a sigh of relief. Let's go to the earnings side then, because maybe that's not quite the sigh of relief. Obviously, the AI trade very much in focus across earnings. High bar for growth. We're in the heart of it right now. What are we seeing? How do you feel about the sustainability of everything? Lee Coppersmith: So, so far you've seen a mixed bag. I think the implied moves heading into this earnings season were all roughly fair, about in line with recent averages over the last few quarters. The main takeaway for us is that AI demand remains incredibly strong, but the competition has become more fierce, and so the dispersion around the market's reaction has increased a lot. We saw that yesterday with the two mega cap tech companies. We've seen that over the last, call it, month, both in the US, across Korea, and even in Europe. So I think the bottom line for us is that there's not really much poking at the AI demand story, but there's a lot more focus around the financing and who's the winner and loser going forward. Chris Hussey: All right. I want to touch on that financing side, because there was a little bit of a credit wobble earlier in the month. What do you think about that? Do you see that in the equity option side, these types of credit wobbles? Lee Coppersmith: So, the credit market to us has been very concentrated to the spaces that have much more AI exposure. If you look at the other spaces within credit, they've all been relatively more insulated or contained in terms of the price moves. The equity space has been incredibly great at essentially migrating some of the volatility to only specific pockets. S&P only really drew down two and a half percent, call it peak to trough. So I think within credit, again, back to this point around who's going to fund this AI build-out, that's the main focus. And when you think about the amount of issuance so far in 2026, it's about three times higher than it was in 2025. And so I think the full story as it relates to credit is this supply versus demand story is getting way more over-tilted towards supply versus demand, and I think that's really the kind of main story here that's kind of leading to wider credit spreads. Chris Hussey: It's been an interesting dynamic, though, because one of the sort of lessons of the post-pandemic equity boom has been that demand has always kept up with supply, no matter where you've been. In fact, demand has led supply. So it'll be interesting to see how that plays out. One of the elements of demand that has been an interesting part of the AI trade has been the retail investor. In June in particular, you saw a lot of demand there sort of pushing a lot of the mega cap tech trade up. Where's that retail investor now? Were they flushed out? Lee Coppersmith: So retail activity has cooled. I wouldn't say that they've completely abandoned the AI trade or the market as a whole, but if you look at volumes today on average versus where we were in late June, volumes from the retail community are down roughly, call it, 20%. So I think what you're saying right now is essentially the sponsorship has waned a little bit because the excitement around the right tail distribution has come in. The same way we've seen our institutional client base buy less call options, we're seeing the same thing happen with retail essentially. So, the one area where we are still seeing some dip buying has been in the leveraged ETF space. Those volumes remain pretty strong. But in terms of the options market, we're not seeing the same type of call buying activity that we once were. Chris Hussey: So if we have this decline in call buying activity, we have this decline in the options market in terms of demand, I would imagine that's pretty good for the price of options. What are you seeing in terms of the hedging community? Are they sort of diving in and taking advantage of this? Lee Coppersmith: Yeah, I think when you kind of back up, the main story for most of this year has been buying calls for sure and people trying to play for this explosive right tail distribution. Really since the end of the summer, most of the pullback in implied volatility, the way the options market's pricing distributions, has mainly been because people have been taking risk down more so on the call option side, not because of put buying. What's happened more recently in the last, call it, few weeks, is we have seen this debate become more two-sided and put buying has picked up, which tells us there's a lot more nervousness around just how things will play out between now through year-end. To us, though, when you think about what the market's implying, the distributions are now pretty fair on both ends. And so because the absolute level of vol isn't very high, we actually think it's a pretty good time to be deploying capital through the options market to be expressing these between now through year-end just because the catalyst path is so rich. Chris Hussey: Is there any risk that we have sort of a self-fulfilling prophecy, though, here? As the market stays flat or drifts a little lower, there's no sort of reward for having bought calls and so you start buying puts and it just, you know, so the more the market is flat, the worse the options market is. Lee Coppersmith: There is definitely a case to be made around that. I think what we've seen now is we've been in this amazingly large consolidation pattern at the index level. However, under the surface, things are realizing. And so, the main theme that we've seen continue to resonate in our world in the option space has been dispersion. Now, it's completely evolved from where we were, call it, in Q1 and Q2 of this year, mainly because you had the momentum factor working on a really high sharp. What's happened really since then is that the momentum factor itself has seen a lot more dispersion. And so like everything else this year, we've just seen, again, a new trend take place where you have to get even more surgical with the way you think about implementing any of your exposure through options particularly. Chris Hussey: Yeah, that seems to be the theme of this conversation here, right? We have dispersion in fundamentals as competition picks up in the AI trade, and we have dispersion in the market that is helping to play that. Okay, put a bow on it. What's the trade? Lee Coppersmith: I think the easiest place to go hunt right now is particularly outside of the AI space. We like biotech here. Lee Coppersmith: We think it's a space that offers a lot of secular properties, just like some of the AI trades previously. But now there's this window where you could potentially have a tailwind of lower rates, more M&A, and I do think the added layer of maybe more drug discovery going forward as a result of some of these AI companies could help lend itself to having more capital get attracted to that area. Chris Hussey: Lee, terrific. Always a wealth of information. Really appreciate you joining us. Chris Hussey: Before I go, I want to make one comment. 45 years ago, I discovered that my mother had breast cancer. Since that time, my family has rallied around Breast Cancer Awareness Month, which comes every October, to help raise money for a cure. You've seen me wear pink throughout October. I encourage everybody to go out there, support breast cancer awareness, and the research that's working towards a cure. That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening. title: The Outlook for US Housing in 2027 amid Rising Mortgage Rates - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Rising mortgage rates are likely to outweigh a longstanding housing shortage in the US next year, leading to a drop in both the sales of existing homes and the construction of new ones, according to Goldman Sachs Research. “In 2027, we expect the headwind from affordability to increasingly dominate, weighing further on activity,” economists Ronnie Walker and David Mericle write in a report. They project that existing home sales will total just 3.9 million in 2027, modestly below their forecast of 4 million for 2026 but 26% below 2019 levels. Against the backdrop of slower home sales, they forecast another year of “anemic” home price growth: 0.8% December-over-December in 2027 after 1.1% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2025. Borrowing costs are a key component of housing affordability. This year’s jump in mortgage rates—in response to the Iran War, higher oil prices, and the prospect of rate hikes by the Federal Reserve—has reduced incentives for homeowners to sell. More than 95% of mortgage borrowers have interest rates below current market rates, and 65% have rates two percentage points below market rates, creating a “lock-in” effect that is slowing sales. In order to purchase a new home, such homebuyers would need to prepay their current mortgage and take out a new mortgage at a higher rate. “The combination of mortgage borrowers refinancing at low rates en masse in 2020 and 2021 and the high current level of mortgage rates has created a significant financial cost to moving,” Walker and Mericle write. Rates for 30-year mortgages in the US have climbed to 7.32% (as of October 22). Goldman Sachs Research’s credit strategists expect mortgage rates to decline in 2027 but remain elevated at 6.4%. Even if that decline is realized, affordability will remain at historically poor levels. Beyond next year, Goldman Sachs Research expects existing home sales to gradually edge higher, reflecting the natural decay of the lock-in effect that comes from, for example, borrowers paying down their mortgages. The renewed popularity of adjustable-rate mortgages in the post-pandemic period could theoretically accelerate this process as well. As rates on such mortgages reset, they tend to erode the impact of the lock-in effect, as seen in other countries where adjustable-rate mortgages are more prevalent. But that impact is likely to be modest in the US, especially over the next couple of years. Adjustable-rate mortgages represent less than 10% of all outstanding mortgages in the US, and only a small share of them will begin to reset in the coming years. Housing activity as measured by residential fixed investment (RFI)—a component of gross domestic product that includes new home construction—is likely to begin recovering by next summer after an expected decline in the months ahead. After posting an estimated 3.1% annualized increase in this year’s third quarter, RFI is forecast to contract by 2.5%, 4%, and 1% annualized in the three quarters that follow, respectively. Thereafter, our researchers expect activity to rebound to a 1-2% growth pace starting in the second half of next year, reflecting the impact of declining mortgage rates. If rates remain at current levels instead, that would lower their RFI growth forecasts by one to two percentage points through the end of 2027. The longstanding housing shortage has kept single-family homebuilding resistant to higher interest rates. Single-family starts have averaged 3% higher than above 2019 levels despite mortgage rates that are three-and-a-half percentage points higher today. This year, however, they have declined by 3% compared with last year, and the slippage is likely to continue. Goldman Sachs Research expects single-family starts to total 0.87 million in 2027 compared to an estimated 0.90 million in 2026. Our economists point to the increase in the available supply of housing, as well as the corresponding compression of margins for homebuilders back to pre-pandemic levels. The elevated pace of homebuilding in recent years has eased historically tight supply-and-demand balances. When the available supply of housing improves, it tends to increase homebuilders’ sensitivity to affordability constraints. Prior analysis by Goldman Sachs Research shows that the higher the vacancy rate was the year before, the more sensitive housing starts are to mortgage rate increases. The combination of still-solid supply growth and slightly weaker demand should push the homeowner vacancy rate higher in the months ahead, from 1.2% in this year’s second quarter to 1.4% by the fourth quarter of 2027. Housing demand is being buoyed by domestic demographic trends that remain supportive, along with real income growth that is likely to accelerate next year, and “build-to-rent” housing, which typically involves a partnership between single-family rental companies and homebuilders to construct rental homes. But on the negative side, survey-based measures of purchase intentions have declined in recent months. Our economists also expect that reduced immigration will continue to weigh on household formation. “We expect housing demand to remain tepid,” Walker and Mericle write. title: This Used Lexus Has A 467-HP V8 And Costs Half Of Its Original MSRP - Top Speed
content: You wouldn’t know it by their current lineup, but Lexus used to be the king of sedans. They actually started their brand with a full-size luxury limousine, the Lexus LS. Then, dealers called on Lexus to give them a slightly more accessible, reasonably priced sedan. Lexus responded with the ES. Then, in 1991, Toyota wanted a luxury sedan similar to Italian luxury sedans for their domestic market in Japan. It was originally dubbed the Toyota Aristo. It was such a hit that by 1993, it moved to selling internationally with a name badge switch to the GS 300. By the early to mid-2010s, the Lexus GS had already hit icon status and was a cult hit among auto enthusiasts. From the start, it was available with either a six-cylinder or a more powerful V8 engine. While there doesn’t seem to be any announced new version of the now venerated GS coming back anytime soon, there is still a lot of interest in the used market. While things are heading in the direction of electrification and turbocharged power, the GS still offers analog capabilities that the market is still looking for. We’re going to go over the necessary things to look out for if you’re interested in this future classic. First and foremost, the Lexus GS F is a luxury sedan. We already know that. The GS F is not only luxurious but also a powerful brute, predicated on its now nearly extinct powertrain. While the United States market only received an inline six-cylinder engine that made 220 horsepower, the rest of the world was already getting the V8. We received the first generation V8 here by 1998. These, however, were just regular luxury sedans with a big V8. They weren't necessarily "F" standard and didn't have any of the performance features you would come to expect. The second generation was the first Lexus GS to technically get the “F” treatment, even if it wasn’t referred to as such. That moniker belongs to the 2016 model and later. You could still get a V8 in the GS 460 from 2008 to 2011, but it wasn’t nearly as powerful. The 2016 to 2020 model is where the true power lies, as it’s tied to a massive naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 that outputs an impressive 467 horsepower and 389 pound-feet of torque. Even more impressive is its reported zero to 60 MPH time of just 4.4 seconds. This is also a high-revving engine that can achieve 7,100 RPM. The Lexus “F” badge on any Lexus represents the legendary Fuji Speedway in Japan. With that in mind, Lexus pulls out all the technological stops to give it the best quality sport handling you would come to expect from a mid-size sport limo. Tethered to the V8 is an eight-speed Sport Direct Shift automatic transmission that also has a manual mode. As you’d probably expect, this also has RWD, but what you might not expect is that it’s equipped with a torque vectoring differential. This allows you to choose from Standard, Slalom, and Track modes. Finally, there are Brembo brakes, a multi-link rear suspension with adaptive dampers, and a double wishbone suspension. Music to our ears. Typically, within the first five years of any mid-size luxury sedan, they lose between 45 and 60 percent of their original MSRP value. Basic economics suggest that the market just doesn’t want mid-size luxury sedans. Everybody wants an SUV, in the US at least. It's even evident in the fact that Mercedes-AMG just released their first-ever GT SUV. Sport variants of any vehicle typically hold their value slightly more than their standard counterparts, but the market is still not entirely there for luxury sedans. You would, however, be shocked to see how well the GS F holds its value. While other sedans are losing their value at a steep decline in five years, a 2016 model, for example, still retains about 44 percent of its original value, according to Kelley Blue Book. The 2018 and 2020 models aren’t that far off either, with 2018 at 48 and 2020 at 55 percent respectively. If we were to follow that same order, the original MSRPs were $85,345 to $86,035 max. Now, they're valued between $41,800 and $47,100 depending on the year, mileage, condition, and the like. It’s ended up (in the American market at least) mainly competing with the likes of the BMW M5 and Mercedes-AMG E63. Other competitors for the regular sedan include the Audi A6. If we’re talking pricing, Kelley Blue Book puts the 2018 BMW M5 at about $41,500 give or take. The AMG E63 of the same year is around $57,770, even closer to $49,000. Both the Mercedes and the BMW have more power and better traction with all-wheel drive, but the Lexus GS F has a naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 that most enthusiasts want. Most enthusiasts want that 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8 because of the simplicity it offers from a maintenance standpoint. Not only that, but at the end of the day, it is considered a Toyota and is often viewed as more reliable from a maintenance standpoint. Not to take away from the Lexus brand itself, because as a standalone, it has achieved the number one spot on JD Power’s most reliable brand list for years and years. At the end of the day, however, this is still a sport sedan, and you will have to pay Sport Sedan pricing for maintenance. Repair pal suggests that the Lexus GS F shows an annual maintenance cost of around $499. This, of course, is dependent on how much you drive it, or whether you actually end up tracking it, as performance tires are often more expensive. That number of $499 also seems awfully low considering this is a more special edition than your standard model. This thing is also heavy at a curb weight of 4,034 pounds. That means you'll be changing the Brembo brakes more frequently. Be sure to ask wherever you're buying this from for a complete maintenance history, especially regarding oil changes and spark plug replacements.​​​​​​​ Although this might be a Lexus, that doesn’t mean that it comes without issues. There was a fuel pump recall for the 2016 to 2018 models, so be sure to check the VIN to confirm whether the recall was addressed or whether it affected that specific model at all. Some blog websites have reported that the carbon fiber trim has lost some of its clear coat as well. The price points for this specific model can vary wildly. You also shouldn’t necessarily buy the newest and lowest mileage one, as maintenance plays a huge role in the quality of your GS F. We’ve even seen some on Cars.com that are going for $70,000 to $90,000. If you find a model in that price range, you could also opt for the newer IS 500, which also has a 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8. However, you might not necessarily want that, as the cabin is much more cramped. The Lexus GS offers more space, comfort, and convenience. We want to hear from you. The company immediately blocked external access upon detecting the breach and is currently conducting a detailed investigation into the scope and extent of the leaked information per customer. Suspected leaked data includes customers’ names, genders, dates of birth, mobile phone numbers, email addresses, residential addresses, and reservation system passwords. Given that many users reuse passwords across multiple online platforms, additional damage from password leaks is also a concern. title: GS Retail signs MOU with veterans ministry to expand social contribution programs - 헤럴드경제
content: GS Retail announced Friday it has signed an MOU with the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to expand social contribution activities aimed at honoring and supporting national merit holders. The agreement, titled the "Patriots and Veterans Social Contribution MOU," was signed Thursday at the Memorial Hall of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea in Seodaemun-gu, Seoul, with Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs Minister Kwon O-eul and GS Retail CEO Heo Seo-hong in attendance. The MOU builds on a decade of "love for the nation" initiatives GS Retail has carried out since launching a Dokdo awareness campaign in 2017, formalizing those efforts into an ongoing social contribution program. The company has also designated veterans support as one of its core social contribution themes this year. Under the agreement, GS Retail and the ministry plan to pursue three initiatives: practical support for national merit holders and their families, activities to raise awareness of the contributions of independence movement figures, and employee volunteer programs. As a first step, GS Retail will support the installation of smart information boards as part of the ministry's "Seeing Independence Merit Holders Clearly" project. The boards provide the public with information on the lives and achievements of lesser-known independence movement contributors. The Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs has installed smart information boards at more than 50 gravesites of independence merit holders since August. GS Retail plans to fund the installation of boards at 18 additional gravesites located outside national cemeteries. The company will also provide daily necessities and food to national merit holders and their families, and will work with the Independence Hall of Korea to give children from immigrant backgrounds opportunities to learn about and experience the history of the independence movement. GS Retail will also formalize regular volunteer activities for its employees. The company plans to use its nationwide stores — including GS25 and GS The Fresh locations — as well as its mobile app to continue raising awareness of veterans commemorations and the contributions of independence movement figures.

title: GS Group Hackathon: 900+ Solve Field Challenges with AI - 조선일보
content: Generative AI solutions developed for real-world operational issues at 5th annual event GS Group has positioned artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies alongside eco-friendliness as the twin pillars of its future innovation strategy, accelerating AI transformation centered on field operations. The plan involves integrating AI technology into traditional core businesses to restructure competitive advantages. GS Group holds an annual Silicon Valley-style idea competition, the "GS Group Hackathon," to spread a culture of AI innovation across the group. Employees from all affiliates participate, developing solutions that apply AI to solve real-world challenges on-site. ◇900+ People Gather to Solve Field Challenges with AI The 5th GS Group Hackathon, held in September at the Westin Seoul Parnas in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, focused on the theme "‘Play with GenAI’ Season 3: Build & Act." This emphasized creating functional AI-driven results for immediate application in work and business operations, rather than merely proposing ideas. The event drew 923 participants, including 797 GS affiliates employees and 126 external participants. Over 1.5 days, participants defined problems, derived solutions, and built initial generative AI-based services. They tackled tasks using "AI-ready data"—refined datasets that AI can instantly learn and analyze. Raw data from business sites like power plants and convenience stores often lack standardized formats, making processing time-consuming. To address this bottleneck, GS has systematically refined data accumulated across its diverse operations. The internal innovation team "52g" has organized tacit knowledge, such as the expertise of skilled workers at GS Donghae Power, into AI-readable formats. They are also developing a "power plant-specific model" that understands on-site workflows. GS plans to leverage this foundation to create industry-tailored AI solutions. The GS Group Hackathon has evolved with technological and operational changes. Launched in 2022 as a digital problem-solving event, it began integrating generative AI in 2024 and opened to external companies in 2025. Cumulative participation since its inception reaches 2,732 people. ◇GS Caltex Optimizes Processes with In-House AI Development Affiliates are also driving AI-driven innovation. GS Caltex is advancing operational transformation through "Digital & AI Transformation (DAX)," which integrates digital and AI transitions. At its Yeosu plant, the company developed in-house AI models to optimize production processes using vast operational data. Previously reliant on workers’ expertise to address process anomalies, the AI now detects early signs of issues and provides real-time solutions. GS Engineering & Construction fosters a culture of free AI use among employees. It became the first domestic construction company to adopt OpenAI’s enterprise AI solution, "ChatGPT Enterprise." Additionally, the company holds an "AI Recipe" competition to enhance employees’ AI proficiency. GS Retail promotes field-centric AI transformation. It established a system to analyze customer feedback (VOC) from convenience stores, home shopping, and supermarkets using generative AI, identifying improvement tasks. The company also formed "AX Cells" to empower field staff with generative AI tools for projects like redesigning the "Franchisee Information Sharing System," which provides tailored data to convenience store owners. Training, workshops, and AI platforms are provided to support this initiative.

title: GS Caltex Kicks Off New Season with Home Opener, Sparki Debut - 조선일보
content: Team unveils AI cheer song, championship ceremony, and interactive fan events at Jangchung Gymnasium [OSEN=Cho Eun-hye Reporter] The GS Caltex Seoul Kixx volleyball team opens the new season against Korea Expressway Corporation. Led by head coach Lee Young-taek, GS Caltex will hold the home opener of the HK Insurance 2026-2027 V-League at Jangchung Gymnasium in Seoul on the 31st. Having warmed up in high spirits with their victory at the 2026 Yeosu·NH Nonghyup Pro Volleyball Tournament, GS Caltex will kick off the new season with strengthened organizational power and a winning DNA, starting a vigorous challenge for the new season in front of home fans. For this home opener, GS Caltex will present a variety of rich and colorful events to offer fans new sights and enjoyable experiences. First, before the game starts, the team will hold a 'Championship Trophy Ceremony' to commemorate their V-League and KOVO Cup victories from last season, allowing home fans to relive the glory of their championship and solidify their resolve for the new season. Following that, the team will unveil their new mascot, 'Sparki,' at the venue for the first time. The newly introduced 'Sparki' will interact with fans both inside and outside the venue, aiming to elevate the cheerful atmosphere of home game cheering. This home opener will also debut the 'AI Cheer Song,' a fan-participation content utilizing AI technology. The 'AI Cheer Song' is a special service that allows fans to create their own customized cheer songs by combining various options such as their preferred player, music genre, and mood. GS Caltex plans to sing the cheer songs created by fans together on-site, adding to the heated atmosphere of the home opener. Additionally, a goods event will give away specially produced 'signed ball keyrings' to the first 1,000 spectators in commemoration of the past championship's emotional victory. The differentiated space design that encourages fan participation also catches the eye. Inside Jangchung Gymnasium, a cabinet-style photo zone has been set up, allowing fans to freely change props, stickers, magnets, and other items inside the cabinets to take their own special commemorative photos. GS Caltex plans to operate the photo zone by changing the decoration props and goods lineup for each round throughout the season, ensuring that fans can experience new content and enjoyable activities every time they visit the venue.
